sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Middletown, NJ?
sections.html:
Middletown Township sells like a large shore suburb with one gate every seller passes through: a Residential Certificate of Occupancy that the township says must be issued before title transfers. Start that inspection early, then fit the rest of the sale around it.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 67,135 residents, and its 2020 to 2024 survey counts 25,211 households. About 85.7 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, the median owner value is $608,300, and median household income is $141,810. Workers spend an average of 34.9 minutes getting to their jobs, which fits a township built around commuter rail, ferries and the Garden State Parkway.

sections.h2: How big is Middletown Township, and where do its sections sit?
sections.html:
Middletown is the largest municipality in Monmouth County, with 67,106 people at the 2020 census. Its 58.72 square miles include 40.95 of land, and roughly 30 percent of the total area is water along Raritan Bay and Sandy Hook Bay. The Sandy Hook peninsula belongs to the township even though it is not joined to the rest of Middletown by land.

Addresses read "Middletown," but local descriptions use section names. The township's own forms list Belford, Chapel Hill, Fairview, Harmony, Leonardo, Lincroft, Locust, Middletown Village, Monmouth Hills, Navesink, New Monmouth, North Middletown, Nut Swamp, Oak Hill, Port Monmouth and River Plaza. Lincroft is the largest of the census designated places, at 7,060 people in 2020.

The township was formed on October 31, 1693, alongside Shrewsbury and Freehold, and incorporated under the 1798 Township Act. A railroad junction in 1875 turned fishing and farming villages into a commuter suburb, and the Seabrook-Wilson House of 1663 and Marlpit Hall of 1686 still stand. Houses from different eras carry different electrical, plumbing and addition histories, so pull the permit record before the inspector arrives.

sections.h2: What does Middletown require before a house changes hands?
sections.html:
Middletown requires a Certificate of Occupancy before transfer of title, and the township's application form warns that violators may face fines or a summons. The same form covers a sale or a rental, goes to the Housing Department at 1 Kings Highway, and asks for the block, lot, number of bedrooms and the prospective transfer date. If the house is occupied, an adult must be home for the inspection, and the form says the visit time depends on the inspector's daily workload.

Charges printed on the Middletown certificate of occupancy application

Source: Middletown Township Application for Residential Certificate of Occupancy (revised October 10, 2025) and the township Fire Prevention page.

The township also lists a 60-Day Conditional Residential Certificate of Occupancy form. Ask Building & Inspection at (732) 615-2104 whether it fits a sale where the buyer plans to make repairs after closing.

sections.h2: What does the Middletown inspector look for?
sections.html:
The township's checklist follows the International Property Maintenance Code and says it is not all inclusive, so other items can be noted on the day. Open permits need a final inspection, and recent construction needs approvals before a certificate can issue.

  • Address numbers at least 4 inches high, readable from the street.
  • A water heater relief valve discharge pipe ending no more than 6 inches above the floor, in copper, galvanized, black or CPVC pipe. PVC is not permitted.
  • Ground fault outlets in the garage, outdoors, on kitchen counters, in unfinished basements and in bathrooms, plus no extension cords in place of wiring.
  • Handrails where stairs have more than four risers, and guards on any open side more than 30 inches above grade.
  • A metal flex hose on the dryer, working burners on the range and no leaks or missing shingles on the roof.
  • A debris-free yard, no peeling exterior paint, a septic system that is not visibly failing, and a self-latching 48 inch barrier around any pool deeper than 24 inches.

Smoke detector and carbon monoxide compliance is now inspected by the Fire Prevention Office at 732-615-2270, and the township's Building & Inspection Department issues the certificate once every requirement is met.

sections.h2: How do buyers see Middletown's location?
sections.html:
Buyers rank Middletown by how it gets them to New York, and the township offers more than one route.

  • Rail: NJ Transit's Middletown station sits on the North Jersey Coast Line between New York Penn Station and Bay Head.
  • Ferry: NY Waterway runs from a slip in Belford, a trip of roughly 50 minutes to West Midtown, and SeaStreak sails from neighboring Highlands to Pier 11 and East 35th Street.
  • Roads: Garden State Parkway exits 109 and 114, Routes 35 and 36, and County Routes 516 and 520, across 350 miles of local, county and state roadway.
  • Bus: NJ Transit local routes 817, 833 and 834.

Health care is close at hand. Memorial Sloan Kettering has a regional center in Middletown, and Bayshore Medical Center in Holmdel and Riverview Medical Center in Red Bank serve the area.

sections.h2: How do schools and shoreline weather affect a Middletown listing?
sections.html:
The Middletown Township Public School District serves pre-kindergarten through grade 12 with 16 schools and 8,895 students in 2023-24. Its three middle schools are Bayshore, Thompson and Thorne, and the two four-year high schools are Middletown High School North and South. Students can also apply to High Technology High School on the Brookdale campus in Lincroft and the Marine Academy of Science and Technology on Sandy Hook, and Christian Brothers Academy is a private option in Lincroft.

The township averages about 46.75 inches of precipitation a year, with July highs near 83 degrees and January lows near 27. A buyer's inspector will look hard at roofs, gutters and grading as a result. The township's certificate page mentions elevation certificates for new construction in mapped flood zones, so ask the township floodplain manager whether your lot sits in one.

sections.h2: How do Middletown property tax appeals and the transfer fee work for a seller?
sections.html:
Monmouth County follows an alternative assessment calendar, so an assessment appeal must be received, not just postmarked, by the County Tax Board on or before January 15. A separate petition goes in for each parcel, the owner needs three to five comparable sales, and hearings run from January through April. The county guide adds that taxes themselves cannot be appealed, only the assessment, and a change-of-assessment postcard gives 45 days to file.

The state charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. Under the state's rate table for sales over $350,000, a sale at the Census median value of $608,300 comes to about $5,273. Deeds above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee of 1 percent to 3.5 percent of the full price, and deeds between spouses, parent and child, or from an estate to an heir are among the listed exemptions.

sections.h2: Where does a Middletown deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for Middletown are recorded with the Monmouth County Clerk in Freehold. The clerk's fee list shows $40 for the first page of a deed, $10 for each additional page and $10 for a marginal notation, and it states that transfer tax must be paid when the deed is recorded. Mortgage discharges are $30 for the first page and $10 for each added page, so ask your closing agent which pieces are being filed.

The clerk also posted a notice that deeds over $1,000,000 received after July 10, 2025 may be subject to a revised transfer fee under P.L. 2025, c. 69. Anyone selling a higher priced home should confirm the amount with the Division of Taxation before closing.

faqs.q: How much does a Middletown certificate of occupancy cost?
faqs.a: The township application lists $150 for each house sold, plus a $15 filing fee on a separate check. A reinspection at the third inspection costs $75. Fire Prevention handles the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate as part of the same process.

faqs.q: Who issues the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate in Middletown?
faqs.a: The Middletown Fire Prevention Office issues it. The township says the certificate is now a component of the Residential Certificate of Occupancy and is sent to Building & Inspection, which issues the CO once everything is met.

faqs.q: What is the Middletown deadline to appeal an assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is January 15. Monmouth County uses an alternative calendar, and the petition must be received by the County Tax Board, not just mailed, with separate paper copies to the assessor and municipal clerk.

faqs.q: Can a Middletown house with open permits still sell?
faqs.a: It can go under contract, but the township's checklist says open permits must have a final inspection before a certificate of occupancy can issue. Ask Building & Inspection for the permit history before you list so no surprises delay the closing.

faqs.q: Which office records a Middletown deed?
faqs.a: The Monmouth County Clerk records it. The posted fee is $40 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, and the seller's Realty Transfer Fee is paid at the time of recording.
